messages:
maria: Heads up — multiple customers reporting 500s from hosted inferencing (/v1/generate) starting ~09:10 UTC. Support ticket IDs attached.

maria: Quick repro I ran: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rw-medium","input":"hello"}' -v
# response: HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
{"error":"internal"}
```

support-jamie: Customer says this started after a config push ~09:05. Some requests succeed, others 500. Latency complaints too.

oncall-bot: @maria @eli assigned to on-call: @eli (eng-oncall) — priority P1.

eli: I'm seeing a sharp spike in quota-orch errors around 09:09. Quota-orch returning 502/504 to gateway -> gateway surfaces 5xx to customers. Metrics: quota-orch p95 latency 1.8s -> 9.2s, error rate 5xx jumped from 0.1% to 6%.

pras: Traced a few traces: quota-orch -> auth-cache (redis) calls timing out. The timeout path is throwing an upstream error and not translating to a 4xx.

ingrid: To confirm: the intended behavior is that when quota check fails due to client limits it should return 429, but when the quota service itself has a dependency timeout we should map to 503/504 for infra. Right now the gateway returns 500/502 because quota-orch is bubbling raw error.

eli: Right. Problem: quota-orch catch-all wraps it and returns 500. For rate-limited customers we expect 429. But these are dependency timeouts (auth-cache redis), so we need clearer mapping: dependency timeout -> 502 up -> should be retriable fallback route or degrade to canary model, not 429.

sre-jen: I pulled traces (trace IDs x-tn-11 -> x-tn-17). Example span: 
```
quota-orch.check() -> call auth-cache.get(key) -> socket timeout after 1500ms -> error: ETIMEDOUT -> quota-orch -> throw upstreamError(status=502)
```

maria: Support workaround: told affected customers to retry after 30s. Also enabled a temporary route rule to skip quota check for internal trusted keys (non-prod) — reduced customer noise but not acceptable long term.

pras: Root cause looks like a recent redis client upgrade changed default socket timeout from 500ms -> 1500ms and combined with a small connection pool caused head-of-line waits under burst. Rolling back that client change stops the 5xx cascade.

ingrid: Immediate mitigations: (1) rollback redis client patch in quota-orch (PR #4021), (2) add mapping so quota-orch returns 429 for explicit rate-limit decisions and 502/504 for dependency timeouts, and (3) add a short-circuit fallback in gateway: if quota-orch returns 502 with known redis timeout signature, route to low-tier model instead of surface 5xx.

eli: I filed a hotfix PR to revert client change, testing in staging now. ETA 30m. Also opening an action item to update quota-orch error mapping and add unit tests for mapping logic.

support-jamie: Customers notified. Escalation note: include timeline, mitigation steps, and planned rollback.

maria: Can someone own postmortem? Prefer eng + support collab.

prs: I'll own the postmortem and include mitigation tickets (rollback, error-mapping, pool-sizing). Will post a draft in #postmortems after rollback validated.

eli: Update 09:45 UTC — hotfix rolled to prod, 5xxs dropped back to baseline, redis timeouts resolved for current bursts. Monitoring for recurrence.

maria: Closing loop with customers, marking incident as resolved for now. Follow-ups: improve canary for client upgrades, add synthetic tests for quota-orch redis latency, and map errors correctly. :white_check_mark:
